# freight-audit-lab

By [Shreyansh Agrawal](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shreyansh2003/) · [Code](https://github.com/shreyansh2003/freight-audit-lab) · Live dashboard: [dashboard link] · Synthetic data; every dollar figure is an estimate. Built with help from Claude.

A simulated freight invoice audit and month-end accrual pipeline. It generates {{scale.shipments|int}} shipments and {{scale.invoices_received|int}} invoices from {{scale.carriers}} invented carriers, seeds them with billing errors and traps (invoices that look wrong but are not), audits them, and accrues unbilled freight.

## The comparison

The baseline lacks business context by design, so the question is which context matters and how much, not whether spreadsheets are bad. It has the engine's rules, tolerances and fuel check and strips BOL formatting, but lacks effective dates, reweigh certificates, authorization timing, and which invoices a rebill replaced.

| | Precision | Recall | False flags |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Engine | {{engine_vs_baseline.overall.engine.precision|pct}} | {{engine_vs_baseline.overall.engine.recall|pct}} | {{engine_vs_baseline.overall.engine.fp|int}} |
| Baseline | {{engine_vs_baseline.overall.baseline.precision|pct}} | {{engine_vs_baseline.overall.baseline.recall|pct}} | {{engine_vs_baseline.overall.baseline.fp|int}} |

Recall is nearly the same; precision is not. A false flag is a dispute the carrier rejects. Its {{baseline_fp_causes.total|int}} false flags each have one cause: rate amendments {{baseline_fp_causes.causes.rate_amendment.false_flags|int}}, late authorizations {{baseline_fp_causes.causes.late_authorization.false_flags|int}}, reweigh certificates {{baseline_fp_causes.causes.reweigh.false_flags|int}}, rebills and balance dues {{baseline_fp_causes.causes.rebill_balance_due.false_flags|int}}, weight errors re-flagged as rate errors {{baseline_fp_causes.causes.weight_misread_as_rate.false_flags|int}}, BOL typos or dropped zeros {{baseline_fp_causes.causes.bol_typo_or_zero.false_flags|int}}, other {{baseline_fp_causes.causes.other.false_flags|int}}. Missing context, not string cleaning.

## Read the engine's numbers with care

Near-perfect engine precision is expected: I built the generator and the engine, so it knows the world it is tested on. It shows coherent logic, not survival on real invoices.

1. **Where the baseline fails.** Its duplicate flags were {{baseline_duplicates.false_share|pct0}} wrong ({{baseline_duplicates.false_flags|int}} of {{baseline_duplicates.flags|int}}), {{baseline_duplicates.share_explained_by_rebills_and_balance_due|pct0}} of the wrong ones from rebills and balance-due invoices.
2. **Where the engine misses.** It missed {{engine_misses.missed|int}} injected errors, {{engine_misses.below_tolerance|int}} of them below its own tolerances, worth {{engine_misses.missed_true_dollars|usd}} (answer-key dollars). No tolerance change clears the {{assumptions.min_material_gain|usd}} materiality bar (an estimate; best gain {{recommended_tolerances.largest_gain_estimate|usd}}), so all {{recommended_tolerances.swept}} stay.
3. **The systemic-issue test.** {{systemic.strongest.carrier_name}} was flagged on {{systemic.strongest.flagged|int}} of {{systemic.strongest.invoices|int}} fuel surcharges shipped {{systemic.strongest.window_start|month}} to {{systemic.strongest.window_end|month}}, against {{systemic.strongest.other_carriers_rate|pct}} at the other truckload carriers ({{systemic.strongest.p_value|pval}}). Each overcharge is about {{systemic.strongest.mean_flag_dollars_estimate|usd}} (estimate): the pattern is the finding. The test also flagged {{systemic.n_others}} weaker pattern (a high-error carrier): triage, not proof.
4. **The accrual diagnosis.** Linehaul and fuel accruals are close to exact by construction: generator, audit and accruals all price from `contract.py`. Accruals landed {{accruals.net_error_pct_estimate|abspct2}} {{accruals.direction}} eventual payable (mean monthly error {{accruals.mape_pct_estimate|pct2}}, estimates), but months net over- and under-accruals; per shipment the mean error is {{accruals.shipment_mape_pct_estimate|pct}}, and {{accruals.shipment_share_over_band_pct_estimate|pct0}} of shipment-months miss by over {{assumptions.large_shipment_error_pct|pct0}}. Accessorials were {{accruals.accessorial_share_of_accrual|pct}} of accrued dollars but {{accruals.accessorial_share_of_net_error|pct0}} of the net {{accruals.gap_word}}, and {{accruals.late_authorization_share_of_net_error|pct0}} of it is late-recorded authorizations (set by the injected late rate).

## Approach

Generator with traps, four carrier layouts, normalization and matching, re-rating, rules, scoring against a sealed answer key, month-end accruals. The answer key is sealed from audit and accrual code (a test enforces it); an accrual at M uses only what was known at M.

## Limitations

- Synthetic data with injected error rates, so the recoverable estimate ({{recoverable.total_estimate|usd}}, {{recoverable.pct_of_billed_estimate|pct2}} of billed) is circular, not a finding.
- Invented formats; no undercharges, in-transit accruals or scale noise (so no weight-tolerance calibration).
- The engine's {{engine_misses.engine_false_positives}} false flag is a typo'd BOL that matched no shipment; left in.

## With real data I would

Ingest EDI 210 and PDF invoices, calibrate tolerances on dispute outcomes, use carrier fuel tables, and add undercharges.

## Run it

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m freight_audit_lab.run
streamlit run streamlit_app.py
```
